title: Migration completeness is unmeasurable: an estate can be un-migrated or leave thousands of files stranded and nothing reports it
body:
## Summary

A fleet audit on 2026-08-26 (devbin/vc, at hv's instruction) measured every Intent project on the machine. The migration is not failing on correctness so much as on VISIBILITY: there is no command that answers "is this estate done?", so an estate can be entirely un-migrated, or migrated and leaving thousands of files stranded, and nothing anywhere says so until a human runs `organize` by hand in that tree.

hv found this by running `intent organise` in four projects in a row and getting a different kind of bad answer each time.

## Measured

22 Intent projects. Snapshot 2026-08-26 20:25:27Z, taken with the release build at pair 03470c5a. Counts move while the bucket-prose carry runs, so these are readings, not fixed facts.

| estate | version | unclaimed | row loss |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Conflab | 2.19.0 | NOT MIGRATED, 123 threads on v2 canon | -- |
| Lamplight | 3.0.0 | 3740 | 10 |
| Laksa | 3.0.0 | 831 | 2 |
| Intent | 3.0.0 | 199 | 0 |
| Courses/002 Agentic Coding | 3.0.0 | 16 | 0 |
| Baize | 3.0.0 | 13 | 0 |
| Anvil | 3.0.0 | 7 | 0 |
| Arca/arca_notionex | 3.0.0 | 7 | 0 |
| Intentv2 | 2.19.0 | frozen v2 by design | -- |
| 13 others | 3.0.0 | 0 | 0 |

13 of 22 are clean on both measures. The residue is concentrated in three estates and 12 genuine row losses sit in two.

## Three distinct defects, and only one of them is data loss

**1. No fleet-level completion measure.** Conflab was simply missed. It declares 2.19.0, carries 123 threads of v2 canon the v3 binary refuses to read, and was last touched 20 hours before the audit. Nothing reported it. Every other estate had either been migrated or was deliberately held with a stated reason -- Conflab was neither, and the only way to find that out was to walk the tree by hand.

**2. The v2 bucket is left unclaimed with no supported close-out.** `organize` correctly reports the pre-v3 `intent/st/{COMPLETED,CANCELLED,NOT-STARTED}/` directories as unclaimed, because the v3 model has no slot for them. But they are NOT duplicates: on Devbin, 22 of 54 bucket files existed nowhere else, `design.md` (74393 b, 26 D-numbered decisions) among them, with 0 of 8 sampled distinctive lines present in either canon JSON, and nine live documents citing those paths as the answer to "why is it built this way?".

The only close-out available on the day was to move the files by hand and repoint the citations, which is what Devbin did (`intent/st/COMPLETED/` -> `intent/history/`, content digest identical either side, 10 citations repointed, 54 -> 0 unclaimed). That is a per-project manual operation with no tool support and no record that it happened.

**3. Citations dropped silently from multi-criterion rows.** A test row citing two criteria migrates carrying one. The row arrives, the AT is green, every id count matches, and the second citation is gone -- where another AT covers the same criterion, the coverage gap is masked too. 10 instances on Lamplight, 2 on Laksa. Lamplight ST0275 is the worst: 7 rows, 6 of which went 1->0, losing every citation they had.

This class was invisible to every check in place until an arm was built for it on the evening of 2026-08-26. Both pre-existing accounting arms count IDS, so a row that arrives with the right id and the wrong covers list is structurally undetectable by them.

**The joiner is not the discriminator.** The defect was first reported with a `+` separator (`-- covers AC-13.2 + AC-13.3 --`). All 26 of Devbin's multi-citation rows use a COMMA. A checker or migrator fix keyed on `+` finds nothing on Devbin and reports it clean. Count distinct `AC-\d+\.\d+` in the covers clause and never parse the joiner.

## What no command currently answers

- Is estate X migrated? (`organize` refuses with a good message, but only from inside that tree)
- Did estate X's migration lose anything? (needs an external accounting instrument)
- How many estates are left? (nothing aggregates)

## Two smaller findings from filing this issue

`intent issues add` creates the record with an empty `body` and there is NO verb that can set one. `sync --to-disk <ID>` resolves IDs as steel threads only -- `sync --to-disk 0098` returned `error: no steel thread ST0098 in this project`. This body was therefore written directly into `intent/.canon/issues/0098.json`, which is the store rather than a generated view, but bypasses the API gate that `sync --to-store` describes. 56 of 77 issues carry bodies; all of those predate v3 and came through the migration.

Separately: the `intent` first on PATH is the brew keg at 3.0.0 `80d8b2ca`, which serves 0 rules, so every critic gate reached through PATH is armed with nothing and exits 0. Known, on the rollout runbook, closing at 3.0.1. Recorded here only because it is the reason write verbs during this rollout must use an absolute path.

## Reported by

devbin/vc, from a full-machine audit at hv's instruction. Devbin and Arca/arca_config are both closed out and clean as of this filing; the instrument used is `intent/whiteboard/vc/at-accounting.sh` in the Devbin estate (three arms: AT ids, AC ids, covers citations; source always read from a git ref, never the working tree).
